sections.h2: How does selling a house in Peachtree Corners, GA work?
sections.html:
Peachtree Corners homeowners can list with a broker, handle a private sale, or take an as-is cash offer, and the right choice often turns on the house's age and condition. The Census Bureau puts the city at 42,519 residents on July 1, 2025, only 0.6% above its April 2020 base of 42,259, which describes a settled, mostly built-out city instead of a fast-growing one.

The 2020 to 2024 Census survey shows 17,799 households, a 53.0% owner-occupied rate and a median owner-occupied value of $484,700. Median gross rent is $1,701, and 29.7% of residents age five and older speak a language other than English at home. With 16.11 square miles of land and 2,623 people per square mile, buyers here compare condos, townhomes and single-family houses within a short drive of each other, so a pricing opinion should come from comparable sales in your own subdivision.

sections.h2: What is Peachtree Corners like, and how did it form?
sections.html:
The area was farmland until the late 1960s, when Technology Park Atlanta was planned as a campus for high-tech employers. Neighborhood builders followed in the late 1970s, starting with Spalding Corners and Peachtree Station. Residents voted for cityhood on November 8, 2011, and municipal operations began on July 1, 2012, making Peachtree Corners the 16th and largest city in Gwinnett County at the time.

The city covers about 17 square miles in the southwest corner of the county, with seven miles of the Chattahoochee River along its western edge. Interstate 85, Interstate 285 and Georgia 400 are all close, and the city describes itself as about 30 minutes northeast of Atlanta. Local landmarks help buyers place a house:

  • Curiosity Lab, a city-owned testing ground with a 3-mile autonomous vehicle track inside a 500-acre technology park
  • Town Center, a 21-acre development at 5200 Town Center Boulevard with shops, restaurants, more than 70 townhomes and a Town Green
  • River parks that offer trout fishing, kayaking and boating on the Chattahoochee
  • Gwinnett County Public Schools, including a STEM school, plus private and parochial options

sections.h2: Does Peachtree Corners charge city property tax?
sections.html:
The city says it keeps a zero millage rate and levies no property tax of its own. Gwinnett County bills the property, and the Tax Commissioner's guide says Peachtree Corners residents get a single combined bill that carries city and county charges. Because the bill may still list service fees, read each line before you quote carrying costs to a buyer.

One fee is specific to the city. Peachtree Corners replaced neighborhood-by-neighborhood streetlight assessments with two citywide rates, $60 a year for residential properties and $180 for commercial ones, and the city says an owner is not charged both the old and new amounts. Streets that adopted speed humps also carry a small annual assessment in that district, which shows up on the tax bill. Ask the seller of any house you are buying, or your own closing attorney, to check whether either charge applies to your parcel.

On timing, the Gwinnett Tax Commissioner says bills are typically mailed in August or September and due in October or November. A late balance gains 0.81% interest each month and a 5% penalty after 120 days, with further 5% steps up to 20%. The 2026 guide also notes that partial payments are accepted if the balance is paid by the due date.

sections.h2: Who handles what for a Peachtree Corners house?
sections.html:
City Hall, Gwinnett County and the state each own a piece of the services around a home, so it helps to know whom to ring.

Police and fire services come to the city from Gwinnett County through intergovernmental agreements. Several major roads, including Buford Highway, Jimmy Carter Boulevard, Peachtree Parkway and parts of Holcomb Bridge Road and Peachtree Industrial Boulevard, are state routes, so a pothole report on those goes through the Georgia Department of Transportation.

sections.h2: What home rules should a Peachtree Corners seller check?
sections.html:
Peachtree Corners enforces a property maintenance code on owners and landlords alike. Exterior items include weeds above 12 inches, inoperable or unlicensed vehicles, dirty pools and spas, damaged fences and trash accumulation. Rentals must meet interior standards covering plumbing, heat, handrails, light and ventilation, and the city's rental-property rules put the duty to fix leaks, electrical hazards and broken windows on the owner.

Trees need special care. A homeowner may remove a tree without a permit unless it stands in a required zoning buffer, conservation area, open space, the Chattahoochee River Corridor or a designated tree save area, or qualifies as a specimen tree. The city defines a specimen as a hardwood of 28 inches or more, a softwood of 30 inches or more, or a native flowering tree of 12 inches or more, measured 4.5 feet above ground. A lot within 2,000 linear feet of the river is in the corridor, and owners must keep at least two live trees. There is no permit fee, although mitigation costs may apply to a landmark or specimen tree.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax bill when a Peachtree Corners house sells?
sections.html:
Gwinnett's rule is built around January 1. Whoever owns the house on that date owes the whole year, and a sale later in the year sends a bill to both parties. Unpaid taxes lead to a lien against the January 1 owner unless proof that the buyer assumed the tax arrives within 90 days after the due date, the deed names the buyer and the deed is recorded.

Ask the closing attorney to use wording like "Seller assigns the liability for the payment of property taxes to the purchaser and purchaser accepts such assignment." The commissioner rejects vague wording such as "Unpaid taxes not accounted for in the closing statement are the responsibility of the seller and buyer to prorate." When tax is paid on time, no documentation is needed.

sections.h2: What does a Georgia deed transfer cost in Peachtree Corners?
sections.html: The Department of Revenue sets the real estate transfer tax at $1 for the first $1,000 of sale price and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fraction of $100. The seller is liable by law unless the contract hands the cost to the buyer. The clerk of superior court must collect it and certify payment before recording the deed. Confirm Gwinnett's recording fees with the clerk, and ask your closing attorney to e-file the PT-61.

sections.h2: Should I list, sell myself, or take a cash offer in Peachtree Corners?
sections.html:
A broker listing tends to produce the strongest price on a house that shows well, and Peachtree Corners buyers typically expect updated kitchens and clean permit records. A private sale works if you can price and negotiate it yourself. A cash buyer purchases without repairs or showings, which suits an inherited house, a tenant-occupied property or a deadline.

Gather your records first: warranty deed, recent tax bill, any permits and the HOA documents if the house belongs to one. Then ask each buyer for a written offer that states price, closing date, who pays transfer tax and how property taxes will be assigned. Weigh the net amounts side by side, not the headline prices.

faqs.q: Does Peachtree Corners have its own property tax?
faqs.a: The city says it maintains a zero millage rate. Gwinnett County bills your property, and your bill may also carry service fees such as the citywide streetlight fee of $60 for residential parcels. Call the Tax Commissioner at 770-822-8800 for the lines on your account.

faqs.q: Who do I call about trees on my Peachtree Corners lot?
faqs.a: Call Public Works at City Hall, 678-691-1200. Permits are needed for trees in buffers, conservation areas, tree save areas, the river corridor and for specimen trees, and a lot must keep at least two live trees.

faqs.q: What happens to my tax bill if I sell in the middle of the year?
faqs.a: Gwinnett sends bills to both the January 1 owner and the buyer. The January 1 owner remains on the lien unless assumption proof, the new deed and recording are completed within 90 days of the due date.

faqs.q: How long can I appeal a Gwinnett assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date printed on the annual Notice of Assessment. Real property questions go to the Assessors at 770-822-7200, and the homestead application should arrive by that same deadline.

faqs.q: Who responds to emergencies in Peachtree Corners?
faqs.a: Gwinnett County police and fire serve the city under agreements with the city. Call 911 in an emergency and 770-513-5700 for non-emergency police matters.
